title: Probability of missing a polynomial on the Boolean cube
statement: Let $n,\\ell,m$ be natural numbers, and let $c$ assign a coefficient in $\\mathbb F_2$ to each subset of $[n]$ of size at most $\\ell$. Form the polynomial on $\\mathbb F_2^n$ whose monomials are the products of the coordinates indexed by those subsets, with coefficients given by $c$. For a uniformly random $m$-tuple of points of $\\mathbb F_2^n$, the probability that this polynomial vanishes at every sampled point equals the $m$th power of the fraction of points in $\\mathbb F_2^n$ at which it vanishes.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ assigns an $\\mathbb F_2$ coefficient to each subset of $[n]$ of size at most $\\ell$
